skills.read.note: Settings lists the served skills by name and description; their text and reference files cannot be opened.

jobs.resolve.note: No lookup of a job by URL, external key or title and company. Job details open Possible duplicates (`jobs.duplicates`) instead.

sources.run.note: Run once, also for one source, sends a bulk action.

sources.delete.note: Remove, also for one source, sends a bulk action.

applications.staleness_list.note: Badges use `stale_inputs` in the application list; details use the per-application report. There is no workspace-wide staleness view.

jobs.create.note: `raw` and `source_key` are collector fields for scripted imports.

applications.create.note: Starting an application sends the job only; plan fields and questions are edited afterwards (`applications.update`).

contexts.create.note: The context dialog sends `template_ids`; `template_id` is the single-template form of the same input.

profile.update.note: `metadata` is edited as rows under Other details; the owner's rules and facts are items of the Policy. The deprecated `preferences` and `roles` stay editable under a collapsed heading.

templates.update.note: The Rules tab edits the typed limits, the rule statements and the free-form rest of `rules` as rows.

applications.update.note: Answers have one control per question; raw JSON is the advanced fallback.

applications.list.note: The Ready to apply queue filters by `readiness=ready` with `sort=ready`; Today's Waiting for a reply and Record replies filter Applied by `applied_until`. The other time ranges serve agents and scripts.

runs.start.note: Runs belong to API tokens: a dashboard session has no runs. Activity shows runs, their reports and their changes read-only.

runs.update.note: Runs belong to API tokens: a dashboard session has no runs.

runs.finish.note: Runs belong to API tokens: a dashboard session has no runs.

events.list.note: The Activity timeline filters changes by who made them (owner, API tokens or one token, system, not recorded), by kind of record (`subject_types`), by period and by run; the job, application and subject filters serve the record histories, agents and scripts.

runs.list.note: Activity filters runs by status; Today lists the runs active since the last visit (`active_since`). The workflow, token and start-time filters serve agents and scripts.

questions.list.note: Today and Activity filter questions by state; `answered_since` and the subject filters serve the agent's next run.

questions.ask.note: Agents ask questions for the owner; the dashboard answers and withdraws them.

requests.take.note: Agents take, complete and decline requests with an API token; the dashboard writes and withdraws them.

requests.complete.note: Agents take, complete and decline requests with an API token; the dashboard writes and withdraws them.

requests.decline.note: Agents take, complete and decline requests with an API token; the dashboard writes and withdraws them.

requests.list.note: Activity filters requests by state and the Ask your agent dialog by subject; `run_id` and `updated_since` serve agents.

requests.read.note: Activity renders requests from the list, which returns complete records.

questions.read.note: Activity renders questions from the list, which returns complete records.

policy.add.note: The form sends the fields it shows; `position` and `idempotency_key` serve agents and scripts (a new item goes to the end, then the arrows move it).

policy.read.note: The screen reads the whole policy; `GET /policy/{section}` serves agents that need one section.

runs.read.note: The report counts all changes of a run and names the records of the first 100 (`changes_limit`); its link opens the timeline filtered by the run, which pages through every change. `changes_offset` serves agents and scripts.
